name: Sanlúcar de Barrameda (Spain)
description: Horizontally divided crimson red over yellow by a blue wavy stripe, the red charged with the crowned arms of Sanlúcar de Barrameda (a ship and a castle on red within an inscribed bordure).
history: The flag of Sanlúcar was created in 1999 by the local journalist and writer José Carlos García Rodríguez, who used the municipal arms as its central motif; it was entered in the Andalusian catalogue of symbols of local entities in 2004 (Boletín Oficial de la Junta de Andalucía no. 246 of 22 December 2004) as a rectangular flag of 2.5 by 1.5 units divided perpendicular to the staff into two stripes, the upper crimson red with the official arms centred on it.
